journeys.title: Chat application
journeys.question: Where does a streamed answer go after I reload?
journeys.outcome: The user message is stored before generation; chunks arrive before completion; the final answer is recoverable without duplicate messages.
journeys.failure: Disconnect the model or lose an acknowledgement, then repair and inspect partial versus completed messages.
journeys.boundary: Synthetic tokens and explicit conversation ownership. Stored-stream recovery is not resuming interrupted model computation.

steps.label: Authorize, read history and save prompt

journeys.title: Video distribution
journeys.question: How can one asset serve thousands of viewers?
journeys.outcome: Cold requests reach the origin; warm segments come from cache or available peers. Compare delivered bytes and playback delays.
journeys.failure: Reduce peer availability or upload capacity and watch missing segments fall back to CDN/origin.
journeys.boundary: Viewer cohorts aggregate thousands of viewers. Peer assistance is a bounded synthetic transport model, not actual WebRTC, ICE, encryption or relay implementation.

journeys.title: Agent trajectories
journeys.question: Which task is waiting, and what happens after a worker crashes?
journeys.outcome: Named tasks execute dependencies and publish status records. Attempt IDs and effects remain distinct during recovery.
journeys.failure: Crash a worker after an effect, then repair it and inspect retry reconciliation and downstream completion.
journeys.boundary: Synthetic task workers and tool calls, not live AI or private chain-of-thought. Recorded events explain observable actions.

journeys.title: Spark-style data job
journeys.question: What happens between map, shuffle and reduce?
journeys.outcome: Inspect task partitions, stage barriers, shuffle/spill costs and actual reduced URL counts.
journeys.failure: Lose an executor, then observe which task results must be recomputed and whether the final counts still match.
journeys.boundary: A bounded Spark-style model, not Apache Spark itself or a calibrated Spark performance predictor.

journeys.title: Social feed
journeys.question: How does a post reach the right followers?
journeys.outcome: Persist posts and follow relations, deliver fanout work, inspect deduplicated timeline entries, and read a user feed.
journeys.failure: Delay fanout or duplicate delivery; compare feed freshness and write amplification for push versus pull.
journeys.boundary: Generic educational social backend, not Twitter infrastructure or its ranking/recommendation algorithms.

steps.label: Publish and read as a user

journeys.title: Workspace permissions
journeys.question: Who can read or change this project task?
journeys.outcome: Inspect workspace, user, project, task and membership records. Follow an access decision and its policy version.
journeys.failure: Revoke membership while a permission cache is warm; compare cached permission with authoritative version checks.
journeys.boundary: Explicit illustrative role and membership policies, not the complete Asana access model or production authentication.
